title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 84 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 478–480 (Night 84, continuing directly from nights-83), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 84 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The old woman closes her sayings of al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa and passes on Sufyān al-Thawrī's counsel to ʿAlī al-Sulamī; she then settles in the king's palace with the five slave-girls, wins his awe by her devotions, and names her price for them, a month's fast, giving him a sealed jug to break it with, until dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالثَّمَانُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-rābiʿatu wa-al-thamānūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fourth and the eighty,
sentences.i: And when it was the eighty-fourth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ قَالَ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-wazīra dandāna qāla li-ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words.

sentences.t: قَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ لِوَالِدِكَ كَانَ الْإِمَامُ الشَّافِعِيُّ يَقُولُ وَدِدْتُ أَنَّ النَّاسَ يَنْتَفِعُونَ بِهَذَا الْعِلْمِ عَلَى أَنْ لَا يُنْسَبَ إِلَيَّ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: qālati al-ʿajūzu li-wālidika kāna al-imāmu al-shāfiʿiyyu yaqūlu wadidtu anna al-nāsa yantafiʿūna bi-hādhā al-ʿilmi ʿalā an lā yunsaba ilayya minhu shayʾun
sentences.l: The old woman said to your father: The imam al-Shāfiʿī used to say: I would love that the people benefit by this knowledge, on condition that nothing of it be ascribed to me.
sentences.i: The old woman said to your father: Imam al-Shāfiʿī used to say, “I wish people would benefit from this knowledge, provided that none of it is ascribed to me.”

sentences.t: وَقَالَ مَا نَاظَرْتُ أَحَدًا إِلَّا أَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ يُوَفِّقَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لِلْحَقِّ وَيُعِينَهُ عَلَى إِظْهَارِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla mā nāẓartu aḥadan illā aḥbabtu an yuwaffiqahu allāhu taʿālā li-al-ḥaqqi wa-yuʿīnahu ʿalā iẓhārihi
sentences.l: And he said: I never disputed with anyone but that I loved that God the exalted should grant him success for the truth and help him to its manifesting.
sentences.i: He also said, “I have never debated with anyone without wishing that God Most High would guide him to the truth and help him bring it to light.”

sentences.t: وَمَا نَاظَرْتُ أَحَدًا قَطُّ إِلَّا لِأَجْلِ إِظْهَارِ الْحَقِّ وَمَا أُبَالِي أَنْ يُبَيِّنَ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ عَلَى لِسَانِي أَوْ عَلَى لِسَانِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā nāẓartu aḥadan qaṭṭu illā li-ajli iẓhāri al-ḥaqqi wa-mā ubālī an yubayyina allāhu al-ḥaqqa ʿalā lisānī aw ʿalā lisānihi
sentences.l: And I never disputed with anyone ever except for the sake of the manifesting of the truth, and I do not care that God make the truth clear upon my tongue or upon his tongue.
sentences.i: I have never debated with anyone except to bring the truth to light, and I do not mind whether God makes the truth plain through my tongue or through his.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ إِذَا خِفْتَ عَلَى عِلْمِكَ الْعُجْبَ فَاذْكُرْ رِضَى مَنْ تَطْلُبُ وَفِي أَيِّ نَعِيمٍ تَرْغَبُ وَمِنْ أَيِّ عِقَابٍ تَرْهَبُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla raḍiya allāhu ʿanhu idhā khifta ʿalā ʿilmika al-ʿujba fa-udhkur riḍā man taṭlubu wa-fī ayyi naʿīmin targhabu wa-min ayyi ʿiqābin tarhabu
sentences.l: And he said, God be pleased with him: When you fear conceit upon your knowledge, then remember the pleasure of him whom you seek, and for what bliss you yearn, and from what punishment you shrink.
sentences.i: He also said, God be pleased with him, “When you fear that conceit will spoil your knowledge, remember whose pleasure you are seeking, for what bliss you long, and what punishment you dread.”

sentences.t: وَقِيلَ لِأَبِي حَنِيفَةَ إِنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ الْمَنْصُورَ قَدْ جَعَلَكَ قَاضِيًا وَرَسَمَ لَكَ بِعَشَرَةِ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ فَمَا رَضِيَ
sentences.tr: wa-qīla li-abī ḥanīfata inna amīra al-muʾminīna abā jaʿfarin al-manṣūra qad jaʿalaka qāḍiyan wa-rasama laka bi-ʿasharati ālāfi dirhamin fa-mā raḍiya
sentences.l: And it was said to Abū Ḥanīfa: Indeed the commander of the believers Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr has made you a judge and decreed for you ten thousand dirhams — and he was not pleased.
sentences.i: Abū Ḥanīfa was told, “The Commander of the Faithful, Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr, has appointed you judge and assigned you ten thousand dirhams.” But he was not pleased.
sentences.n: The words فما رضي (“and he was not pleased”) are about Abū Ḥanīfa; the sentence passes from what was said to him to what he felt.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي تَوَقَّعَ أَنْ يُؤْتَى إِلَيْهِ فِيهِ بِالْمَالِ صَلَّى الصُّبْحَ ثُمَّ تَغَشَّى بِثَوْبِهِ فَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-yawmu alladhī tawaqqaʿa an yuʾtā ilayhi fīhi bi-al-māli ṣallā al-ṣubḥa thumma taghashshā bi-thawbihi fa-lam yatakallam
sentences.l: And when it was the day on which he expected that there would be brought to him in it the money, he prayed the morning, then covered-himself with his garment, and did not speak.
sentences.i: On the day when he expected the money to be brought to him, he prayed the dawn prayer, then wrapped himself in his cloak and said nothing.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَاءَهُ رَسُولُ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِالْمَالِ فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَخَاطَبَهُ فَلَمْ يُكَلِّمْهُ
sentences.tr: thumma jāʾahu rasūlu amīri al-muʾminīna bi-al-māli fa-lammā dakhala ʿalayhi wa-khāṭabahu fa-lam yukallimhu
sentences.l: Then there came to him the messenger of the commander of the believers with the money, and when he entered upon him and addressed him, he did not speak to him.
sentences.i: Then the Commander of the Faithful's messenger came to him with the money; but when he came in and spoke to him, Abū Ḥanīfa would not answer.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ الْخَلِيفَةِ إِنَّ هَذَا الْمَالَ حَلَالٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu rasūlu al-khalīfati inna hādhā al-māla ḥalālun
sentences.l: And the caliph's messenger said to him: Indeed this money is lawful.
sentences.i: The caliph's messenger said to him, “This money is lawful.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ اعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ حَلَالٌ لِي وَلَكِنْ أَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَقَعَ فِي قَلْبِي مَوَدَّةُ الْجَبَابِرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla iʿlam annahu ḥalālun lī wa-lakin akrahu an yaqaʿa fī qalbī mawaddatu al-jabābirati
sentences.l: And he said: Know that it is lawful for me, but I dislike that there fall in my heart the affection of the tyrants.
sentences.i: He answered, “Know that it is lawful for me; but I dislike the thought that love for tyrants should settle in my heart.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ لَوْ دَخَلْتَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَتَحَفَّظْتَ مِنْ وُدِّهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu law dakhalta ilayhim wa-taḥaffaẓta min wuddihim
sentences.l: And he said to him: If you were to enter to them and guard yourself from their affection —
sentences.i: The messenger said to him, “Suppose you went in to them, and kept yourself guarded against their favour —”

sentences.t: قَالَ هَلْ أَ أْمَنُ أَنْ أَلِجَ الْبَحْرَ وَلَا تَبْتَلَّ ثِيَابِي
sentences.tr: qāla hal a ʾamanu an alija al-baḥra wa-lā tabtalla thiyābī
sentences.l: He said: Am I secure that I enter the sea and my garments not be wetted?
sentences.i: “Can I,” he said, “walk into the sea and not have my clothes get wet?”
sentences.n: The print sets a lone أ before امن (هل أ امن). It is kept as printed and read as أَأْمَنُ, “am I secure…?”; the form is doubtful, but the sense — that one cannot go among rulers and stay untouched — is plain from the reply.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ كَلَامِ الشَّافِعِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-min kalāmi al-shāfiʿiyyi raḍiya allāhu taʿālā ʿanhu
sentences.l: And from the speech of al-Shāfiʿī, God the exalted be pleased with him:
sentences.i: And among al-Shāfiʿī's sayings, God Most High be pleased with him:

sentences.t:
اَلَا يَانَفْسُ اَنْ تَرْضَىٰ بِقَوْلِيْ * فَاَنْتِ عَزِيزَةٌ اَبَدًا غَنِيَّه
دَعِيْ عَنْكِ الْمَطَامِعَ وَالْاَمَانِيْ * فَكَمْ اُمْنِيَّةٍ جَلَبَتْ مَنِيَّه
sentences.tr:
alā yā nafsu an tarḍā bi-qawlī * fa-anti ʿazīzatun abadan ghaniyyah
daʿī ʿanki al-maṭāmiʿa wa-al-amānī * fa-kam umniyyatin jalabat maniyyah
sentences.l:
Ah, O soul, if you be content with my word, * then you are dear forever, rich.
Leave from yourself the longings and the wishes, * for how-many a wish has brought a death.
sentences.i:
O soul, if you would be content with what I say, * you are precious and rich for ever.
Put aside your greed and your hopes, * for many a wish has fetched death.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all. The first line is read as a condition (“if you are content”). The print ends غنيه with ه for ة, its usual spelling; it rhymes with منية.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ كَلَامِ سُفْيَانَ الثَّوْرِيِّ فِيمَا أَوْصَى بِهِ عَلِيَّ ابْنَ الْحَسَنِ السُّلَمِيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-min kalāmi sufyāna al-thawriyyi fī-mā awṣā bihi ʿaliyya ibna al-ḥasani al-sulamiyya
sentences.l: And from the speech of Sufyān al-Thawrī, in what he charged with it upon ʿAlī son-of al-Ḥasan al-Sulamī:
sentences.i: And among the sayings of Sufyān al-Thawrī, in what he counselled ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Sulamī:

sentences.t: عَلَيْكَ بِالصِّدْقِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْكَذِبَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ وَالرِّيَاءَ وَالْعُجْبَ
sentences.tr: ʿalayka bi-al-ṣidqi wa-iyyāka wa-al-kadhiba wa-al-khiyānata wa-al-riyāʾa wa-al-ʿujba
sentences.l: Upon you the truthfulness, and beware-you of the lying and the betrayal and the ostentation and the conceit,
sentences.i: Keep to truthfulness, and beware of lying, betrayal, showing off and conceit,

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الْعَمَلَ الصَّالِحَ يُحْبِطُهُ اللَّهُ بِخَصْلَةٍ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْخِصَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-ʿamala al-ṣāliḥa yuḥbiṭuhu allāhu bi-khaṣlatin min hādhihi al-khiṣāli
sentences.l: For the righteous deed — God nullifies it by one trait from these traits.
sentences.i: For God voids a righteous deed through any one of these faults.

sentences.t: وَلَا تَأْخُذْ دِينَكَ إِلَّاعَنْ مَنْ هُوَ مُشْفِقٌ عَلَى دِينِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā taʾkhudh dīnaka illā ʿan man huwa mushfiqun ʿalā dīnihi
sentences.l: And do not take your religion except from one who is solicitous over his religion.
sentences.i: And take your religion only from someone who is anxious for his own.
sentences.n: The print runs إلا and عن together (الاعن); they are read as two words.

sentences.t: وَلْيَكُنْ جَلِيسُكَ مَنْ يُزَهِّدُكَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَأَكْثِرْ ذِكْرَ الْمَوْتِ وَأَكْثِرِ الِاسْتِغْفَارَ وَاسْأَلِ اللَّهَ السَّلَامَةَ فِيمَا بَقِيَ مِنْ عُمُرِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-li-yakun jalīsuka man yuzahhiduka fī al-dunyā wa-akthir dhikra al-mawti wa-akthiri al-istighfāra wa-isʾali allāha al-salāmata fī-mā baqiya min ʿumrika
sentences.l: And let your companion be one who makes-you-abstain in the world, and increase the mention of death, and increase the asking-of-forgiveness, and ask God for safety in what remains of your life.
sentences.i: Let your companion be someone who teaches you to renounce this world; keep death often in mind, ask forgiveness often, and beg God for safety in the life you have left.
sentences.n: The print has يزهدل, a misprint for يزهدك, corrected here (ل for ك).

sentences.t: وَانْصَحْ كُلَّ مُؤْمِنٍ إِذَا سَأَلَكَ عَنْ أَمْرِ دِينِهِ وَإِيَّاكَ أَنْ تَخُونَ مُؤْمِنًا فَإِنَّ مَنْ خَانَ مُؤْمِنًا فَقَدْ خَانَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-anṣaḥ kulla muʾminin idhā saʾalaka ʿan amri dīnihi wa-iyyāka an takhūna muʾminan fa-inna man khāna muʾminan fa-qad khāna allāha wa-rasūlahu
sentences.l: And counsel every believer when he asks you about the matter of his religion, and beware-you that you betray a believer, for whoever betrays a believer has betrayed God and his messenger.
sentences.i: Give honest counsel to every believer who asks you about his religion, and beware of betraying a believer, for whoever betrays a believer has betrayed God and His Messenger.

sentences.t: وَإِيَّا كَ وَالْجِدَالَ وَالْخِصَامَ
sentences.tr: wa-iyyā-ka wa-al-jidāla wa-al-khiṣāma
sentences.l: And beware-you of the disputation and the quarrelling.
sentences.i: And keep away from argument and quarrel.
sentences.n: The print splits the pronoun off (ايا ك); it is one word, إياك.

sentences.t: وَدَعْ مَا يَرِيبُكَ إِلَى مَالَا يَرِيبُكَ تَكُنْ سَلِيمًا وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ تَكُنْ حَبِيبَ اللَّهِ وَأَحْسِنْ سَرِيرَتَكَ يُحْسِنِ اللَّهُ عَلَانِيَتَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-daʿ mā yarībuka ilā mālā yarībuka takun salīman wa-ʾmur bi-al-maʿrūfi wa-nha ʿani al-munkari takun ḥabība allāhi wa-aḥsin sarīrataka yuḥsini allāhu ʿalāniyataka
sentences.l: And leave what makes-you-doubt for what does-not make-you-doubt, you will be sound; and command with the known and forbid from the disapproved, you will be the beloved-of God; and make good your inner-self, God will make good your outward-self.
sentences.i: Leave what troubles you for what does not, and you will be safe; enjoin the right and forbid the wrong, and you will be God's beloved; make your inner life good, and God will make your outer life good.
sentences.n: The print runs ما and لا together (مالا, “what — not”); they are read as two words.

sentences.t: وَاقْبَلِ الْمَعْذِرَةَ مِمَّنِ اعْتَذَرَ إِلَيْكَ وَلَا تُبْغِضْ أَحَدًا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَصِلْ مَنْ قَطَعَكَ وَاعْفُ عَمَّنْ ظَلَمَكَ تَكُنْ رَفِيقَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-iqbali al-maʿdhirata mimmani iʿtadhara ilayka wa-lā tubghiḍ aḥadan mina al-muslimīna wa-ṣil man qaṭaʿaka wa-ʿfu ʿammani ẓalamaka takun rafīqa al-anbiyāʾi
sentences.l: And accept the excuse from one who has excused himself to you, and do not hate anyone of the Muslims, and join him who cut you off, and pardon him who wronged you; you will be companion of the prophets.
sentences.i: Accept the apology of anyone who apologises to you; hate no Muslim; keep ties with the one who cut you off, and forgive the one who wronged you, and you will be a companion of the prophets.

sentences.t: وَلْيَكُنْ أَمْرُكَ مُفَوَّضًا إِلَى اللَّهِ فِى السِّرِّ وَالْعَلَانِيَةِ وَاخْشَ اللَّهَ خَشْيَةَ مَنْ قَدْ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ مَيِّتٌ وَمَبْعُوثٌ وَصَائِرٌ إِلَى الْحَشْرِ وَالْوُقُوفِ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ الْجَبَّارِ
sentences.tr: wa-li-yakun amruka mufawwaḍan ilā allāhi fī al-sirri wa-al-ʿalāniyati wa-ikhsha allāha khashyata man qad ʿalima annahu mayyitun wa-mabʿūthun wa-ṣāʾirun ilā al-ḥashri wa-al-wuqūfi bayna yadayi al-jabbāri
sentences.l: And let your affair be entrusted to God in secret and in the open, and fear God with the fear of one who has known that he is dead and raised and bound for the gathering and the standing between the hands-of the Compeller.
sentences.i: Let your whole affair be left with God, in private and in public, and fear Him as one who knows that he will die, be raised, and go to the Gathering to stand before the Almighty.
sentences.n: الجبار, “the Compeller”, is one of the names of God; بين يدي, literally “between the hands of”, means “before”.

sentences.t: وَاذْكُرْ مَصِيرَكَ إِلَى إِحْدَى الدَّارَيْنِ أَمَّا جَنَّةٌ عَالِيَةٌ وَأَمَّا نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-udhkur maṣīraka ilā iḥdā al-dārayni ammā jannatun ʿāliyatun wa-ammā nārun ḥāmiyatun
sentences.l: And remember your destination to one of the two abodes: either a garden lofty or a fire hot.
sentences.i: And remember that you are bound for one of the two abodes: either a lofty garden or a blazing fire.
sentences.n: Both phrases echo the Qurʾān: جنة عالية (69:22) and نار حامية (101:11).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعَجُوزَ جَلَسَتْ إِلَى جَانِبِ الْجَوَارِي فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ وَالِدُكَ الْمَرْحُومُ كَلَامَهُنَّ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُنَّ أَفْضَلُ أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِنَّ وَرَأَى حُسْنَهُنَّ وَجَمَالَهُنَّ وَزِيَادَةَ أَدَبِهِنَّ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿajūza jalasat ilā jānibi al-jawārī fa-lammā samiʿa wāliduka al-marḥūmu kalāmahunna ʿalima annahunna afḍalu ahli zamānihinna wa-raʾā ḥusnahunna wa-jamālahunna wa-ziyādata adabihinna
sentences.l: Then the old woman sat at the side of the slave-girls; and when your father the one-granted-mercy heard their speech he knew that they were the best of the people of their time, and he saw their beauty and their loveliness and the excess of their culture.
sentences.i: Then the old woman sat down beside the slave-girls. When your late father heard them speak, he knew that they were the finest women of their age; he saw their beauty and grace and how far their accomplishments went.

sentences.t: فَأٓوَاهُنَّ إِلَيْهِ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْعَجُوزِ فَأَكْرَمَهَا وَأَخْلَى لَهَا وَلِجَوَارِيهَا الْقَصْرَ الَّذِي كَانَتْ فِيهِ الْمَلِكَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ بِنْتُ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ
sentences.tr: fa-āwāhunna ilayhi wa-aqbala ʿalā al-ʿajūzi fa-akramahā wa-akhlā lahā wa-li-jawārīhā al-qaṣra alladhī kānat fīhi al-malikatu abrīzatu bintu maliki al-rūmi
sentences.l: And he lodged them with him, and turned toward the old woman and honoured her, and vacated for her and for her slave-girls the palace in which the queen Abrīza daughter-of the king of Rūm had been.
sentences.i: He lodged them with him, turned to the old woman and showed her honour, and gave her and her slave-girls the palace where Queen Abrīza, the Byzantine king's daughter, had lived.
sentences.n: The print spells فآواهن without the madda; it is read as “and he lodged them”.

sentences.t: وَنَقَلَ إِلَيْهِنَّ مَا يَحْتَجْنَ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْخَيْرَاتِ فَأَقَمْنَ عِنْدَهُ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَالْعَجُوزُ مَعَهُنَّ
sentences.tr: wa-naqala ilayhinna mā yaḥtajna ilayhi mina al-khayrāti fa-aqamna ʿindahu ʿasharata ayyāmin wa-al-ʿajūzu maʿahunna
sentences.l: And he conveyed to them what they needed of the good-things, and they stayed with him ten days, and the old woman with them.
sentences.i: He had everything they needed carried to them, and they stayed with him ten days, the old woman among them.

sentences.t: وَكُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا يَجِدُهَا مُعْتَكِفَةً عَلَى صَلَوٰتِهَا وَقِيَامِهَا فِي لَيْلِهَا وَصِيَامِهَا فِي نَهَارِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-kullamā dakhala ʿalayhā yajiduhā muʿtakifatan ʿalā ṣalawātihā wa-qiyāmihā fī laylihā wa-ṣiyāmihā fī nahārihā
sentences.l: And whenever he entered upon her he would find her devoted to her prayers, and her standing in her night, and her fasting in her day.
sentences.i: Every time he visited her he found her absorbed in her prayers, standing in worship all night and fasting all day.

sentences.t: فَوَقَعَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مَحَبَّتُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿa fī qalbihi maḥabbatuhā
sentences.l: And there fell in his heart love of her.
sentences.i: And love for her settled in his heart.

sentences.t: وَقَلٰ لِي يَا وَزِيرُ إِنَّ هَذِهِ الْعَجُوزَ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَقَدْ عَظُمَتْ فِي قَلْبِي مَهَابَتُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lī yā wazīru inna hādhihi al-ʿajūza mina al-ṣāliḥāti wa-qad ʿaẓumat fī qalbī mahābatuhā
sentences.l: And he said to me: O vizier, this old woman is of the righteous-women, and there has grown great in my heart her awe.
sentences.i: And he said to me, “Vizier, this old woman is one of the righteous, and my awe of her has grown great in my heart.”
sentences.n: The print has وقل for وقال; this is the edition's habit and the dagger alif marks the reading.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَادِيَ عَشَرَ اجْتَمَعَ بِهَا مِنْ جِهَةِ دَفْعِ ثَمَنِ الْجَوَارِي إِلَيْهَا فَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-yawmu al-ḥādiya ʿashara ijtamaʿa bihā min jihati dafʿi thamani al-jawārī ilayhā fa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: And when it was the day the eleventh, he met her with respect to paying the price of the slave-girls to her, and she said to him:
sentences.i: On the eleventh day he met her to pay her the price of the slave-girls, and she said to him,

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّ ثَمَنَ هَذِهِ الْجَوَارِي فَوْقَ مَا تَتَعَامَلُ بِهِ النَّاسُ فَإِنِّي لَا أَطْلُبُ فِيهِنَّ ذَهَبًا وَلَا فِضَّةً وَلَا جَوَاهِرَ قَلِيلًا كَانَ ذَلِكَ أَوْكَثِيرًا
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-maliku iʿlam anna thamana hādhihi al-jawārī fawqa mā tataʿāmalu bihi al-nāsu fa-innī lā aṭlubu fīhinna dhahaban wa-lā fiḍḍatan wa-lā jawāhira qalīlan kāna dhālika awkathīran
sentences.l: O king, know that the price of these slave-girls is above what the people deal in; for I do not ask for them gold, nor silver, nor jewels, little though that be or much.
sentences.i: King, know that the price of these girls is beyond anything people trade in; I ask for no gold or silver or jewels for them, whether little or much.
sentences.n: The print runs أو into كثيرا (اوكثيرا); they are read as two words. Its تتعامل takes الناس as a feminine singular subject, as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ وَالِدُكَ كَلَامَهَا تَعَجَّبَ وَقَالَ أَيَّتُهَا السَّيِّدَةُ وَمَا ثَمَنُهُنَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa wāliduka kalāmahā taʿajjaba wa-qāla ayyatuhā al-sayyidatu wa-mā thamanuhunna
sentences.l: And when your father heard her speech he was amazed and said: O lady, and what is their price?
sentences.i: When your father heard what she said he was astonished, and asked, “My lady, then what is their price?”

sentences.t: قَالَتْ مَا أَبِيعُهُنَّ لَكَ إِلَّابِصِيَامِ شَهْرٍ كَامِلٍ تَصُومُ نَهَارَهُ وَتَقُومُ لَيْلَهُ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: qālat mā abīʿuhunna laka illā bi-ṣiyāmi shahrin kāmilin taṣūmu nahārahu wa-taqūmu laylahu li-wajhi allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: She said: I will not sell them to you except for the fasting of a full month — you fast its day and you stand its night — for the face of God the exalted.
sentences.i: She said, “I will sell them to you only for a full month of fasting: you fast by day and keep vigil by night, for the sake of God Most High.”
sentences.n: The print has ونقوم, a misprint for وتقوم, corrected here (ن for ت). It also runs إلا into the next word (الابصيام); they are read as two words.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ فَعَلْتَ ذَلِكَ فَهُنَّ مِلْكٌ لَكَ فِي تَصَرُّفِكَ تَصْنَعُ بِهِنَّ مَا شِئْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-in faʿalta dhālika fa-hunna milkun laka fī taṣarrufika taṣnaʿu bihinna mā shiʾta
sentences.l: And if you do that, they are a possession to you in your disposal; you do with them what you wish.
sentences.i: If you do that, they are yours to dispose of as you please — do with them what you like.
sentences.n: The print has تصرك, a misprint for تصرفك, corrected here (the ف is dropped).

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْمَلِكُ مِنْ كَمَالِ صَلَاحِهَا وَزُهْدِهَا وَوَرَعِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-maliku min kamāli ṣalāḥihā wa-zuhdihā wa-waraʿihā
sentences.l: And the king was amazed at the perfection of her righteousness and her abstinence and her scrupulousness.
sentences.i: The king marvelled at how complete her goodness, her renunciation and her scrupulous piety were.

sentences.t: وَعَظُمَتْ فِي عَيْنِهِ وَقَالَ نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهَذِهِ الْمَرْأَةِ الصَّالِحَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿaẓumat fī ʿaynihi wa-qāla nafaʿanā allāhu bi-hādhihi al-marʾati al-ṣāliḥati
sentences.l: And she grew great in his eye, and he said: May God benefit us by this woman, the righteous.
sentences.i: She rose high in his eyes, and he said, “May God let us profit by this righteous woman.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اتَّفَقَ مَعَهَا عَلَى أَنَّهُ يَصُومُ الشَّهْرَ كَمَا اشْتَرَطَتْهُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma ittafaqa maʿahā ʿalā annahu yaṣūmu al-shahra ka-mā ishtaraṭathu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then he agreed with her that he would fast the month as she had stipulated it upon him.
sentences.i: Then he agreed with her that he would fast the month as she had stipulated.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَأَنَا أُعِينُكَ بِدَعَوَاتٍ أَدْعُو بِهِنَّ لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu wa-anā uʿīnuka bi-daʿawātin adʿū bihinna laka
sentences.l: And she said to him: And I will help you with supplications that I call with for you.
sentences.i: She said to him, “And I will help you with prayers that I shall offer on your behalf.”

sentences.t: فَائْتِنِي بِكُوزِ مَاءٍ فَأَتَاهَا بِكُوزِ مَاءٍ فَأَخَذَتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʾtinī bi-kūzi māʾin fa-atāhā bi-kūzi māʾin fa-akhadhathu
sentences.l: Bring me a jug of water. And he brought her a jug of water, and she took it.
sentences.i: “Bring me a jug of water.” He brought her a jug of water, and she took it.
sentences.n: The print has ماو at its second “water”, a misprint for ماء, corrected here.

sentences.t: وَقَرَأَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَهَمْهَمَتْ وَقَعَدَتْ سَاعَةً تَتَكَلَّمُ بِكَلَامٍ لَا نَفْهَمُهُ وَلَا نَعْرِفُ مِنْهُ شَيْأً
sentences.tr: wa-qaraʾat ʿalayhi wa-hamhamat wa-qaʿadat sāʿatan tatakallamu bi-kalāmin lā nafhamuhu wa-lā naʿrifu minhu shayʾan
sentences.l: And she recited over it, and muttered, and sat an hour speaking with speech we did not understand and did not know anything of.
sentences.i: She recited over it and muttered, and for an hour she sat speaking words we could not follow, understanding nothing of them.
sentences.n: The narration slips into “we” here (لا نفهمه), as the print has it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ غَطَّتْهُ بِخِرْقَةٍ وَخَتَمَتْهُ وَنَاوَلَتْهُ لِوَالِدِكَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma ghaṭṭathu bi-khirqatin wa-khatamathu wa-nāwalathu li-wālidika wa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: Then she covered it with a rag, and sealed it, and handed it to your father, and said to him:
sentences.i: Then she covered it with a cloth, sealed it, gave it to your father, and said,

sentences.t: إِذَا صُمْتَ الْعَشَرَةَ الْأُولَى فَأَفْطِرْ فِى اللَّيْلَةِ الْحَادِيَةَ عَشَرَ عَلَى مَا فِي هَذَا الْكُوزِ فَإِنَّهُ يَنْزِعُ حُبَّ الدُّنْيَا مِنْ قَلْبِكَ وَيَمْلَاؤُهُ نُورًا وَإِيمَانًا
sentences.tr: idhā ṣumta al-ʿasharata al-ūlā fa-afṭir fī al-laylati al-ḥādiyata ʿashara ʿalā mā fī hādhā al-kūzi fa-innahu yanziʿu ḥubba al-dunyā min qalbika wa-yamlāʾuhu nūran wa-īmānan
sentences.l: When you have fasted the first ten, break-fast on the eleventh night upon what is in this jug, for it removes love of the world from your heart and fills it with light and faith.
sentences.i: When you have fasted the first ten days, break your fast on the eleventh night with what is in this jug, for it will take the love of this world out of your heart and fill it with light and faith.
sentences.n: The print spells يملؤه with an alif, يملاؤه.

sentences.t: وَفِي غَدٍ أَخْرُجُ إِلَى إِخْوَانِي وَهُمْ رِجَالُ الْغَيْبِ فَإِنِّي اشْتَقْتُ إِلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ أَجِيءُ إِلَيْكَ إِذَا مَضَتِ الْعَشَرَةُ الْأُولَى
sentences.tr: wa-fī ghadin akhruju ilā ikhwānī wa-hum rijālu al-ghaybi fa-innī ishtaqtu ilayhim thumma ajīʾu ilayka idhā maḍat al-ʿasharatu al-ūlā
sentences.l: And tomorrow I go out to my brothers — and they are the men of the unseen — for I have longed for them; then I come to you when the first ten has passed.
sentences.i: Tomorrow I shall go out to my brothers, the Men of the Unseen, for I long to see them; then I shall come back to you when the first ten days are over.
sentences.n: رجال الغيب, “the men of the unseen”, are the hidden saints of popular belief, who are said to move unrecognised among people.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ وَالِدُكَ الْكُوزَ ثُمَّ نَهَضَ وَأَفْرَدَ لَهُ خَلْوَةً فِى الْقَصْرِ وَوَضَعَ الْكُوزَ فِيهَا وَأَخَذَ مِفْتَاحَ الْخَلْوَةِ فِي جَيْبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha wāliduka al-kūza thumma nahaḍa wa-afrada lahu khalwatan fī al-qaṣri wa-waḍaʿa al-kūza fīhā wa-akhadha miftāḥa al-khalwati fī jaybihi
sentences.l: And your father took the jug, then rose, and set apart for it a retreat in the palace, and put the jug in it, and took the key of the retreat in his pocket.
sentences.i: Your father took the jug, got up, set aside a private room in the palace, put the jug in it, and kept the key to the room in his pocket.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ النَّهَارُ صَامَ السُّلْطَانُ وَخَرَجَتِ الْعَجُوزُ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-nahāru ṣāma al-sulṭānu wa-kharajati al-ʿajūzu ilā ḥāli sabīlihā
sentences.l: And when it was the day, the sultan fasted, and the old woman went out to the state of her way.
sentences.i: When day came the sultan fasted, and the old woman went out and went her way.
sentences.n: إلى حال سبيلها is an idiom for “went on her way”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, with its rhyme on -āḥ, as in every night.
